title: Numbers bundle id com.apple.Numbers is likely wrong on macOS
detail: Every Numbers recipe (rule 8, the B21 example) and the builder spec for numbers_script.py (cloud/builder_finance.md:52) use `tell application id "com.apple.Numbers"`. To my knowledge Mac Numbers is `com.apple.iWork.Numbers` (com.apple.Numbers is the iOS bundle id). If so, every Numbers script fails when NSAppleScript compiles it in AppleScriptRunner.run (Skills.swift), or AppleScript shows a modal 'Where is ...?' app chooser during the demo. That breaks all three finance demo tasks.
evidence: iTunes Search API: bundleId com.apple.Numbers belongs to trackId 361304891, kind=software (the iOS app). I could not look up the Mac App Store listing (id 409203825) from this VM, so I have not verified this on a Mac. A 2-second check on the M5: `osascript -e 'id of app "Numbers"'`.
fix: Run the osascript check. If it prints com.apple.iWork.Numbers, replace the id in prompts/planner_system.md:42,71 and cloud/builder_finance.md:52 (and tell the finance builder, so the numbers_script.py golden strings use it). Also add `tell application id "<id>" to get name` to AppleScriptRunner.warmUp so a wrong id fails at app start rather than mid-demo, and so the first Numbers call skips the ~9 s compile.

title: SUMIF example doesn't match the statement's columns, sign or table name
detail: The only budget-formula example the planner sees is =SUMIF(Transactions::C2:C121,"Dining",Transactions::B2:B121). In the fixture CSV, A=Date, B=Description, C=Amount, D=Balance, and there is no category column. That formula matches category text against Amount and sums Description, so it returns 0. Even with a category column, debits are negative, so Actual would come out negative. A CSV imported into Numbers creates a table called 'Table 1', so 'Transactions::' only resolves if the agent renames the table first. The model copies this example literally, so Budget Actual would be 0 or negative while looking correct.
evidence: evals/fixtures/finance/bank_statement_oct2026.csv header `Date,Description,Amount,Balance`. Debits are negative: the rebalanced fixture total spend is 4,112.26, and my Decimal recompute gives Dining actual 347.21, whereas -SUMIF without the sign flip gives -347.21.
fix: Let the engine compute the numbers. Have it write a Category column (E) in one bulk write, rename the table to Transactions, then set Budget!C(n) to `=-SUMIF(Transactions::$E$2:$E$121,A2,Transactions::$C$2:$C$121)`. Read the formula results back and compare them to the engine's Decimal totals to the cent: if they agree, say done; if not, ask. The sheet then shows live formulas a judge can click, which is the 'every action carries evidence' story.

title: Numbers read recipe drops the last row and returns typed values
detail: (a) For a 120-transaction table with a header, `range "A1:D120"` drops sheet row 121 (the last transaction, 10-31). (b) `value of every cell` returns AppleScript date objects and reals, not strings. Coerced to text, dates come out as locale strings ('Saturday, October 24, 2026 at 12:00:00 AM'), so load_statement's ISO parse fails, and amounts arrive as binary floats. (c) The recipe also suggests `sort`. Sorting the statement reorders its rows, so the engine's 1-based row ids no longer point at the right sheet rows, and the duplicate/outlier highlights land on the wrong rows.
evidence: Fixture: 120 data rows + header = A1:D121, which builder_finance.md's own SUMIF uses (C2:C121). Numbers' AppleScript dictionary exposes both `value` (typed) and `formatted value` (displayed string) on cells. Not run on a Mac.
fix: Read with `formatted value of every cell of range ("A1:D" & (row count))` and join it into TSV inside the script, so one Apple event returns one string. Highlight rows by row id before any sort, or write a Row column first and map by that.

title: Already-refunded Amazon duplicate is reported as an open duplicate
detail: The planted AMAZON MKTP -64.99 x2 on 10-21 is reversed by AMAZON MKTP REFUND +64.99 on 10-28. The truth file lists it under `duplicates` without that link, so the engine and mascot will say 'two duplicate charges' and invite a dispute that is already settled. That is wrong advice presented as correct, and a finance judge will catch it. Separately, the `seen` set in build_rows forbids any legitimate same-day, same-amount repeat (for example a BART round trip at the same fare), so the exact-match duplicate rule is never tested against its most common false positive.
evidence: Rows (rebalanced CSV): duplicates [[18,19] UBER, [Amazon pair]], refunds [AMAZON MKTP REFUND 10-28 +64.99]. The truth keys hold no linkage. 21 same-day, same-merchant pairs exist (4 are BART), and none share an amount, by construction.
fix: In the truth file, emit `duplicates: [{rows:[a,b], amount, status:'open'|'refunded', refund_row}]`. In the engine, mark a duplicate pair 'refunded' when a later credit of the same normalized merchant and amount exists. Mascot line: 'Uber $23.47 charged twice on 10/9; the Amazon double charge was refunded 10/28.' Optionally plant one same-fare BART round trip as a hard negative and make the duplicate rule `ask` (not flag) for merchants with fixed fares.

title: Spec's MAD-per-category outlier rule flags 15 normal rows
detail: On the rebalanced statement, Dining is bimodal (40 coffees at $3-6 plus meals), and Transport is mostly $2-4 BART. A robust MAD z-score (>3.5) per category flags every Chipotle, Sweetgreen and DoorDash meal, both Uber rides, the Lyft ride and the Kaiser copay, plus the Apple Store charge. Only the 'absolute floor' separates the real outlier. If the builder tunes the floor until the test passes, the rule is fitted to this fixture. On another statement it either flags lunches or misses a $400 outlier.
evidence: My computation on cloud/finance@6f28fa3 CSV: Dining median 5.34, MAD 0.93, flags rows 9,29,39,40,50,60,70,89,110 (z 5.5-18.0); Transport median 3.00, MAD 0.45, flags 18,19 (UBER z 30.7) and 26 (LYFT z 11.8); Health flags 111 (z 8.5); Shopping flags only 85 (APPLE 1299, z 95). 13 of 28 merchants have fewer than 3 rows, so per-merchant MAD is not usable either.
fix: Use a documented two-part rule: debit >= max($250, 5% of monthly income) AND >= 10x the category median (or a MAD z on log(amount) > 3.5), excluding payroll, rent and recurring. Put both numbers in the evidence string ('$1,299 is 66x your Shopping median of $19.63'). Test it on a second seed with the planted outlier removed, and also on a seed with a planted $400 outlier.

title: Receipt fixture never tests fuzzy names, posting delay; PHILZ trap
detail: Receipts 1-6 use exactly the statement description and date, and candidates are restricted to a merchant+date that appears once. So an exact join passes, and the fuzzy matching and posting-delay handling the spec requires are never tested. Receipt 8 (PHILZ COFFEE, 10-30) also sits between PEET'S COFFEE rows on 10-29 and 10-31 and a BLUE BOTTLE COFFEE row on 10-31. A normalized difflib ratio against PEETS COFFEE is 0.67, so a fuzzy matcher with a ±1-day window would likely report receipt 8 as amount_mismatch instead of no_match.
evidence: receipts.truth.json@6f28fa3: receipt_08 {PHILZ COFFEE, 2026-10-30, 10.58}. CSV rows 106,108,109,118,119 are PEET'S COFFEE and 117 is BLUE BOTTLE COFFEE, all within 2 days. difflib.SequenceMatcher('PHILZ COFFEE','PEETS COFFEE').ratio()=0.67.
fix: Add 2 receipts that keep their match_row in the truth file: one where the receipt reads 'Trader Joe's #127' against the statement's TRADER JOE'S, and one dated the day before it posts. Require at least one distinctive token to match, ignoring generic words (COFFEE, STORE, MKTP, TRIP, RIDE). Add a test that receipt 8 stays no_match.

title: Receipt line items and grocery tax look fake on screen
detail: split_items cuts the subtotal at random points, so receipts show items like OAT LATTE 0.10 and NEW ORLEANS ICED 0.18 (main receipt_07), and FROZEN GYOZA 1.66 next to MANDARIN CHICKEN 13.27 (cloud/finance receipt_07). 10.25% sales tax is also applied to Trader Joe's, Safeway and Berkeley Bowl groceries, but California exempts most groceries. These receipts are shown on screen during the OCR step, and a finance-track judge will notice.
evidence: Rendered receipts/receipt_07.png on main@c09dcbd and cloud/finance@6f28fa3 (viewed).

title: Budget written to Numbers with unresolved asks miscounted
detail: When categories are unresolved (`complete:false`), the CLI still emits write_budget. Without a model, the 'ask' rows go to Uncategorized and drop out of the budget categories. With a model, a low-confidence 'ask' guess (categorize.py:125,127) is counted in category_spend (budget.py:25) and drives over_budget. Either way the agent writes wrong Actual/Remaining numbers before the user answers, which contradicts 'escalate, don't guess'.
evidence: Running `python -m brain.finance analyze --statement bank_statement_oct2026.csv --budget budget_oct2026.truth.json --scripts` gives complete=False, ask BERKELEY BOWL x6, Groceries actual 203.61 vs truth 298.70 (95.09 under), and write_budget still contains 'set acts to {1625.00, 203.61, ...}'. test_cli_without_answers_escalates asserts the write_budget script is emitted in this state.
fix: Leave ask rows out of the actual totals and report them as pending: {pending:{rows,amount}}. Emit write_budget only when complete is true (otherwise emit highlight and an ask). Or write the affected categories' Actual as blank and mark them 'pending'.

title: Receipt mismatch is unbounded; changed charges after posting delay become no_match
detail: Pass 3 claims any same-day, same-merchant debit as amount_mismatch, however far the amounts differ. A changed amount that posts 1-3 days later (restaurant tip, hotel or fuel hold) only matches when the digits are an adjacent swap, so it reports 'No bank charge for receipt N', which is false. The prefix rule also merges distinct merchants.
evidence: Repro (synthetic, f098120): a $5.00 SAFEWAY receipt was matched to a same-day $12.00 row as amount_mismatch. A $15.00 CHIPOTLE receipt with an $18.00 charge posted 1 day later came back as no_match. merchant_match returned True for SAFEWAY~'SAFEWAY FUEL 1444', APPLE~'APPLE ICLOUD' and UBER~'UBER EATS'.
fix: Pass 3: allow a 0-3 day window and require |diff| <= max($1, 25% of total) (tips fit in this). Otherwise no_match, with a 'nearest candidate' hint and not as a statement fact. Prefix match only when the remaining tokens are store or location noise, not category words (FUEL, EATS, ICLOUD).

title: Single-token keywords and tie order miscategorize common merchants
detail: Single words such as RENT, LIME, TOLL and PARKING are matched as whole tokens, ties go to whichever rule appears first in the dict, and COSTCO is filed as Shopping. Recurring categories are also exempt from the outlier check, so a wrong Rent label hides large charges.
evidence: rule_category probes (tests/probe_engine.py): 'RENT THE RUNWAY'->Rent, which makes it exempt from the outlier check. 'KEY LIME CAFE'->Transport (LIME and CAFE tie, and Transport comes first in the dict). 'COSTCO WHSE #123'->Shopping. 'SHELL SERVICE STATION'->None. 'PARKMOBILE'->None.
fix: Break ties toward Dining/Groceries over Transport/Rent, or score by specificity. Require RENT to be the whole description or followed by PAYMENT/PMT. Add SHELL as a fuel keyword when followed by station or numeric tokens. Accuracy on the fixture is unaffected (95% with rules only, the misses are the BERKELEY BOWL asks).

title: Every non-refund credit counts as Income, inflating income and net
detail: Any credit that is not a refund gets INCOME with rule confidence 1.0 and no ask. That includes transfers from savings, Venmo/Zelle reimbursements of a different amount, and card rewards. On a real statement, income and net in the summary table would be overstated and shown as certain.
evidence: Code categorize.py:104-106: `if t.amount > 0 and t.row not in refunds: out[t.row] = (INCOME, RULE_CONFIDENCE, 'rule')`, why='credit:not_a_refund'. rule_category('TRANSFER FROM SAVINGS') is None, yet as a credit it becomes Income at p=1.0.
fix: Only credits that hit an INCOME keyword become Income at p=1.0. Other credits go to 'Transfer/Other credit' with source 'ask' (or call decide()), and are left out of total_income until confirmed.

title: Cash reserve only recognizes a 'lake house down' sentence
detail: cash_excess subtracts a reserve only when a notes sentence contains both 'lake house' and 'down'. That rule fits only the Henderson notes. Any other near-term need (remodel, tuition, home purchase, tax bill) gives a $0 reserve, so the brief tells the advisor to invest money the clients said to keep liquid, and prints 'Lake house: $0.00 down payment next spring.' This is a wrong recommendation presented as computed. The Henderson truth values are correct.

Result: excess 188480.00 (was 68480.00), reserve 0.00. The brief says 'Move $188,480.00 of excess savings to the brokerage and invest at target.' and '- Lake house: $0.00 down payment next spring.' (brief.py:118).

Let the notes parser propose reserves from any sentence with $ + a near-term date or 'keep liquid' and surface them as an ask/confirm. title: Review sheet and prior prep note deleted without confirm
detail: numbers_review_script deletes any existing sheet named 'Review' in the client's workbook, and notes_brief_script deletes every note with the prep title, before writing. 'Review' is a common sheet name in an advisor's own workbook. Under AGENTS.md, overwriting needs `confirm`, and tools_interface.md says tool scripts skip the planner's confirmation policy, so nothing stops it. The demo file is fresh, but on a real workbook this is an unconfirmed destructive action.

Neither is gated by ask_confirm (tools_interface.md: 'tool-generated scripts are trusted code: they bypass the planner's script-confirmation policy').

title: Non-Henderson households: single filers crash, 401(k)/HSA/checking taxed
detail: account_kind only recognizes 'roth', 'ira' and 'savings'. A 401(k), 403(b), HSA or checking account is treated as a taxable brokerage, so its losses become TLH candidates (no tax effect in a 401(k)), its lots become donation candidates, and checking cash counts as invested. roth_room raises KeyError for any status other than MFJ 2026, which kills prep() for every single filer. That status is in the same Rev. Proc. 2025-32 Table 3. The 'get the Garcia household review ready' example in catalog.json would fail outright for a single client.
evidence: tests/probe_advisor.py: account_kind('Mark 401(k)')='taxable', 'Elena 403(b)'='taxable', 'Mark HSA'='taxable', 'Joint Checking'='taxable'. With profile filing_status='single', prep raises KeyError 'no verified bracket table for 2026 single'.
fix: Map account types explicitly (401k/403b/457/SEP/SIMPLE -> traditional, HSA -> tax_free, checking/money market -> liquidity), or require an account-type column and ask when it's unknown. Add the Rev. Proc. 2025-32 single/HoH/MFS 22% tops. If a table is missing, return roth {status:'unverified'} instead of raising.

title: Opportunities ranked by non-comparable 'impact' dollars
detail: The ranking compares dollars moved (rebalance), idle savings, convertible amount, harvestable losses and gains avoided as if they were the same unit. Rebalance ranks first only because it moves the most money, and TLH ranks last even though it is a realized tax benefit. An advisor judge will read 'ranked by $ impact' as value to the client.
evidence: prep() opportunities: rebalance 118151.60 'to move' > cash 68480.00 > roth 61400.00 'convertible' > donate 53472.00 'gains avoided' > TLH 30825.00 'losses harvestable'. None of these are estimated $ benefit.
fix: Rank by estimated annual benefit with a stated rate: TLH loss x LTCG rate (15% MFJ for this income per Rev. Proc. 2025-32), donation gain x 15%, cash excess x (expected return - HYSA), Roth room x (future rate - 22%). Or keep the order fixed and label it 'by size'.

title: merchant_match rejects common receipt-vs-bank descriptor pairs
detail: Extra words on the bank side are allowed only from a short Berkeley-centric NOISE list, and different word counts get no fuzzy fallback. title: Verified-done never sees Numbers script results; answer goals likely rejected
detail: planner-verify (#54, VERIFY_DONE=on by default) accepts `done` only if the last action's expect passed, the skill self-verified, or the done carried a passing expect; otherwise it runs _verify_done. That verifier asks the planner's bool decision 'Is the goal achieved? Judge only from the fresh observation and the actions taken; if any part of the goal is not visibly complete, answer No.' Its state is the goal, actions_log lines cut to 160 chars ('script applescript """tell application id "com.apple.Numbers" ... -> ok'), a fresh AX observation and OCR. It never includes the script output (self._script_output, set at :1934 and consumed by the next plan turn) or the done summary. Rule 8 makes `script applescript` the only way to read Numbers, and its own worked example (planner_system.md:76, 'put the total of column B in B21' -> script returns the total, next turn done) has no expect. So every Numbers question the planner answers from a script ('what's the average amount', 'total of Dining', 'how many rows over $100') reaches the verifier with an answer that is on no screen. A strictly instructed bool judge will likely say No, which triggers _recover / _honest_failure instead of the correct answer. Writes that land in visible cells may pass via AX/OCR, but Numbers' AX table exposure is partial. finance_review does not use this path (brain tool), so the scripted finance demo is unaffected. Planner Numbers fallbacks and live/bench Numbers cases are.

The done branch (:2655-2700) falls through to _verify_done for script-then-done.
